Model conductor elevation along the line

Source: R/risk.R
conductor_profile.Rd

Conductor returns are points the wire rule labelled (label == "wire") or that the classifier calls wire with probability >= min_p_wire. Returns within structure_mask_m of a support are ignored (guy wires, crossarms and insulators there are elevated and linear too). Each bin_m chainage bin takes a low quantile (q) of return elevations; bins below the lower bound (physically non-compliant, so an artefact) or implying a slope steeper than max_slope to both neighbours are rejected. Surviving bins are interpolated across gaps of at most max_gap_m (src = "measured"). Elsewhere the conductor is bracketed (src = "bounded"):

Usage

conductor_profile(
  pred,
  segments,
  dtm,
  supports = NULL,
  step_m = 1,
  search_m = 15,
  min_p_wire = 0.9,
  structure_mask_m = 8,
  bin_m = 5,
  min_bin_points = 3,
  q = 0.25,
  max_slope = 0.2,
  max_gap_m = 30,
  min_ground_clear_m = 4.9,
  attach_m = 20,
  max_span_m = 500
)

Arguments

pred

Output of predict_points().

segments

Output of segment_lines().

dtm

Ground elevation raster (metres), from corridor_rasters().

supports

Optional sf points of support structures.

step_m

Vertex spacing of the conductor model (metres).

search_m

Wire points farther than this from the line are ignored.

min_p_wire

Classifier probability needed for a point the rule did not label to count as a conductor return.

structure_mask_m

Returns this close to a support are ignored.

bin_m, min_bin_points, q

Chainage bin width, minimum returns per bin, and the quantile of return elevations used per bin.

max_slope

Maximum plausible conductor slope (rise / run) between adjacent measured bins.

max_gap_m

Largest gap between measured bins that is interpolated.

min_ground_clear_m, attach_m, max_span_m

Bounds parameters, metres.

Value

data.frame of vertices: line_id, x, y, tx, ty (unit tangent along the line), s_m, seg_id, ground, z_lo, z_hi, src. The attribute bins is a data frame with one row per line counting the chainage bins that held conductor returns (n_bins) and how many each sanity check rejected (n_too_few, n_below_floor, n_implausible), with n_measured the bins that survived, so a profile that silently lost most of its returns can be told from one that never had them.

Details

  • lower bound: ground + min_ground_clear_m. NESC Table 232-1 vertical clearance for a 115 kV line is roughly 4.9 m over land accessible only to pedestrians (more over roads), so a compliant line is not lower.

  • upper bound: with supports, the straight chord between the supports either side of a station, each at ground + attach_m. A conductor sags below the chord between its attachments, so it cannot be higher unless attachments exceed attach_m. Where the next support lies outside the data the upper bound is unknown and set to Inf (no optimistic claim). Without supports, the highest chord between any two points no more than max_span_m apart is used, which is only an upper bound if real spans are no longer than that.

A terrain-following model (constant height above the ground below) is wrong where a span crosses a gully; the bounds make that uncertainty explicit instead of hiding it.
